diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Kayhan newspaper wrote in an editorial that changing the nuclear doctrine and enhancing deterrence could prevent danger to the regime and territorial sovereignty of the country. The newspaper added that if the Islamic Republic had nuclear weapons, its leader would not have been attacked and assassinated in this way. Kayhan also referred to the deterrent role of nuclear weapons in the tensions between India and Pakistan and in North Korea.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the missile and drone capabilities of the Islamic Republic are equivalent to a nuclear bomb. He added that Iran's missile stockpiles have increased by more than 50% and would not be depleted even if the war continues for two years. Boroujerdi also said that the Islamic Republic will not enter negotiations with the US without implementing its seven conditions, and if another war occurs, the response will be harsher and will cause damage to the entire region.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in the Tuesday session of the Islamic Consultative Assembly that Mojtaba Khamenei is in full health and that what was very prominent and influential for him in meeting with him was his strong, lively, and hopeful spirit alongside his firmness and inner calm. Ghalibaf added that the leader's mastery over issues, both in general and in detail, was very remarkable. The speaker also said that during the session, various issues were discussed, including the country's economic matters, and Mojtaba Khamenei carefully followed macroeconomic indicators and emphasized the need for precise attention to these indicators.

Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said that the formation of the next Israeli government may not be achieved even after weeks of negotiations and another election might be held. He also pointed to concerns about the Likud party possibly protesting the election results and disagreements over the assignment of the government formation mission.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, says officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey have traveled to Tehran to try to prevent the expansion of regional conflicts by relying on their defensive capacities and to influence the calculations of the Islamic Republic.

Seyed Mohammad Reza Razavi Fard, a lawyer, was summoned to serve a prison sentence. He was previously sentenced by the Revolutionary Court of Qom to 10 years and one day in prison. According to a notification dated 4 Aban, he was asked to appear within five days to execute the sentence.

The Tehran prosecutor has requested the approval and implementation of a resolution to completely ban men from all women's football matches by sending letters to the Minister of Sports and the Football Federation president. The prosecutor's office cited non-compliance with mandatory hijab and "moral norms and standards" as the reason for this action. This decision has faced strong protests from female players.
Yesterday, Paria Nasiri, a 17-year-old student from Naqadeh, was released on bail.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, stated that the government and other governing bodies are prepared for all possible scenarios and expressed confidence that "with unity, potential crises can be overcome." Mohajerani said the neither war nor peace situation harms the country and must be overcome. The spokesperson added that the government seeks peace with dignity but the armed forces will strongly defend the country if the slightest aggression occurs on its soil.

A video received by Iran International shows a group of students from Gorgan University of Natural Resources gathered on Tuesday, 5 Aban, in the presence of one of the university's deputies to protest the low quality of the cafeteria food.

The "Viona" cafe in Arak has been sealed by order of the Public Places Supervision Department since Monday, 4 Aban. Authorities have not provided an official explanation for the closure as of the report's preparation. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Masoud Shabanzadeh, head of Mes Shahrbabak football team, confirmed the resignation of coach Ghasem Shahba and denied his dismissal. He said two candidates are being considered to replace Shahba. Mes Shahrbabak is at the bottom of the Iranian Premier League table with 5 draws, 5 losses, and no wins.

Qadir Hasanzadeh, the director general of Golestan Environmental Protection, announced that the province needs 1,038 rangers but currently only 129 rangers, about 12% of the required force, are protecting them. He said Golestan province, with about 346,000 hectares of natural areas under management, faces a serious shortage of human resources in environmental protection.

Ahmad Khatami, a member of the Assembly of Experts, said the selection of Mojtaba Khamenei was the work of God and divine will, and all forces and people supported it. He added that Israel intended to target the Assembly of Experts to prevent the leader's selection, and in bombing conditions, the leader had to be chosen quickly. Khatami also said that with a short speech about Trump's disappointment, the Assembly expressed their support.

Several people were arrested in Bampur. Several individuals were arrested during security forces' operations near Bampur county in Sistan and Baluchestan province due to alleged membership in opposition groups.

The Football Federation's Appeals Committee rejected Esteghlal club's appeal and complaint against Mohammad Hossein Kananizadegan. The case was formed following a clash in the 107th derby between Kananizadegan and Aref Aghasi. The Appeals Committee confirmed the disciplinary committee's acquittal ruling due to Aghasi's consent and lack of court-admissible evidence.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that the Tamarchin border in Azerbaijan province, which is the northwestern border of Iran with Iraq, has been closed.

A group of workers from Khosheh Saba Agro-Industry Company, who have been transferred to Mahan Investment Company, gathered on Tuesday, 4 Aban, at their workplace in Khoda Afarin County to protest the non-payment of their several years of overdue claims. These protesting workers demand full payment of their salaries and other overdue claims, which have not been paid despite repeated follow-ups.

German and French media have reported on Iran's role in Israel's election competitions, the disagreement among Benjamin Netanyahu's opponents over the Palestine issue, and the return of tens of thousands of Israelis from abroad to participate in the elections. Ahmad Samadi and Sajedeh Sharifi, journalists from Iran International, report.

Meir Javdanfar, an analyst on Israeli affairs, said forming a 61-seat coalition for Benjamin Netanyahu seems difficult, but the poll results are not definitive. He added that the opposition might form a government with the support of Arab parties, even without their presence in the cabinet.

After the Tehran prosecutor sent a letter to the Minister of Sports and the Football Federation president about a ban on men attending women's football matches, ticket sales for the Persepolis and Esteghlal women's match were stopped. A meeting is being held at the league organization to review the letter, and the match may be held without spectators. The first derby between the two teams is scheduled for Wednesday, 6 Aban, at Ghal'eh Hassan Khan Stadium.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that diplomatic efforts by regional countries will likely not prevent the recurrence of war. He added that while the US seeks to shape a new Middle East order relying on regional actors, the Islamic Republic will not have a place in this order.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, went to a polling station in Jerusalem on Tuesday morning, 5 Aban, to participate in the parliamentary elections and cast his vote. Polls indicate a close competition between the Likud party led by Benjamin Netanyahu and the rival coalition led by Gadi Eisenkot. These elections are held after a tense period in Israel's history, including the Hamas attack on 15 Mehr 1402, subsequent Israeli military operations in Gaza, and internal disagreements over Netanyahu's right-wing government policies.
Gonash Fateh, a resident of Urmia, was released from the city's prison on Saturday, 2 Aban, after posting bail.

British prosecutors announced that two men have been charged in connection with last month's incident at the Royal Air Force Fairford base under the country's national security law. British police believe the country that Mohammad Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran. Mohammad Abdulkarim and Nouman Asghar have been charged with offenses related to aiding a foreign intelligence service and entering a prohibited place, and they are scheduled to appear in court.

Hojjat (Yaser) Moghadam, a resident of Birjand, was arrested on Sunday, 3 Aban, while commuting on a street by agents of the Intelligence Department and transferred to an unknown location. According to HRANA news agency, he faces charges of propaganda against the regime and disturbing public opinion.

Alireza Beiranvand, the national team goalkeeper, officially joined Fajr Sepasi club to serve his military duty and became a student of Mehdi Rajabzadeh. Due to the closed transfer window, Beiranvand cannot play in matches for Fajr Sepasi and must wait until the mid-season transfer window opens to be registered on the team list. On Monday, 4 Aban, he reported to his military unit at Abadeh barracks and received the necessary equipment for the training period.

Simultaneously with the Israeli parliamentary elections, some Iran International viewers have expressed their support for Benjamin Netanyahu in response to election posts. Some have also expressed hope for his victory and called for action against the Islamic Republic.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the Vice Speaker of the Islamic Republic's Parliament, warned that any action by the US against the Islamic Republic will be met with a powerful response and will deeply regret Washington. He said Donald Trump has reached a deadlock on the war issue and is trying to manage internal US problems by lowering oil prices and advancing negotiations. Hajibabaei emphasized that regional security must be ensured by regional countries and the US has no role in providing this security.

Abolfazl Aboutorabi, a member of the Parliament's Councils Commission, said the enemy has threatened to destroy Iran and that Iran must leave the NPT and build an atomic bomb. He added that coordination with the Supreme National Security Council is needed for the plan to leave the NPT. Aboutorabi also said that the tunnels inside Koh-e-Kalang mountain cannot be destroyed even by an atomic bomb and warned that if another war occurs, the world will be set on fire.

On Monday, 4 Aban, a number of independent bakers in Iranshahr went on strike in protest against the reduction of flour quotas and opposition to the increase in bread prices. The protesting bakers considered the current flour quota insufficient and referred to increased operating costs and equipment depreciation. A video showing the suspension of activity of these bakery units was published.

Israel's Central Elections Committee announced that voter turnout had exceeded 16% by 10 AM on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, a figure unprecedented in the last three decades. The Israeli parliamentary elections are taking place in an atmosphere where the competition between Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition parties led by Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett is intertwined with disagreements over the war with the Islamic Republic, Tehran's nuclear threat, and how to confront its proxy groups.

The media office of Mojtaba Khamenei reported that he met with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic. In this meeting, Rezaei presented a report on the country's conditions and the pursuit of the Islamic Republic's strategic policy to organize endogenous regional arrangements and order. The time and place of this meeting were not disclosed.

According to Agence France-Presse, Kylian Mbappé's controversial remarks about Mao Zedong, former leader of China, sparked a wave of anger in the country, leading to the unilateral termination of major commercial contracts and the blocking of the French star's accounts. Prominent Chinese brands cut ties with Mbappé. Three major companies, Dongpeng, Mengniu, and Milkyground, announced the end of their cooperation with the player.
The police commander of Bafq county reported the closure of a cafe and a sports club in the county due to what was described as "non-compliance with Islamic norms and police regulations."
A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that the cost of his car's oil service, including oil and air filters, has reached about 7.5 million tomans.

The UK prosecution announced that two men have been prosecuted near the RAF Fairford base in southwest England. The UK counter-terrorism police say one of the suspects is suspected of cooperating with the intelligence agency of the Islamic Republic. This information was announced as part of ongoing investigations into the security incident in the area.

Reza Pahlavi called Iranians in a video message to prepare to join the "National Cooperation Campaign to Save Iran" and to contact his team via a Telegram account. He identified the Revolutionary Guards as the main cause of Iran's economic and security deterioration and has plans for overthrowing the Islamic Republic and governing the country afterward. Pahlavi also urged military and security forces to join the people and warned that those involved in repression will be held accountable.

Reports from Tabriz, Mashhad, and other parts of Iran describe severe increases in costs and economic difficulties. People report rising healthcare expenses, rent hikes, and insurance problems. It is also reported that some services and goods, such as motor oil, have become scarce and prices have sharply increased.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation issued its verdict regarding the match between Malavan Bandar Anzali and Tractor Tabriz, declaring the result 3-0 in favor of Malavan. Malavan Club was also fined 1 billion tomans and had 2 points deducted due to its fans' behavior. The owner of Tractor Club had previously stated that if the match was ruled 3-0 against Tractor, they would withdraw from the Premier League.

On Tuesday, 5 Aban, a group of retirees and pensioners of Homa Airlines gathered in front of the company's central office in Tehran to protest issues with health insurance and the halt of living and welfare subsidies. The protesters demanded attention to their demands due to ongoing medical problems and increased living costs.

Agence France-Presse reported, citing two Kuwaiti judicial sources, that the criminal court of Kuwait sentenced three men to death for plotting to assassinate the Deputy Prime Minister, collaborating with Iran, and membership in Hezbollah. All three are from the Shia Muslim community, which makes up about one-third of Kuwait's population. The court also sentenced 11 others linked to the case to five years of forced labor.

Seyed Mehdi Razavi-Fard, a lawyer, announced that his 10 years and one day prison sentence has been finalized. He wrote on his X social media account that he must present himself for serving the prison term by next week.

The Football Federation's Appeal Committee rejected Persepolis club's appeal regarding the complaint against Esteghlal over Yaser Asani's presence in their lineup. The committee confirmed the disciplinary committee's ruling acquitting Esteghlal and the player. Persepolis claims Asani had terminated his contract with Esteghlal before the season started.

Prince Reza Pahlavi called on Iranians in a video message to declare readiness to join the "National Cooperation Campaign to Save Iran." He described this period as an opportunity for regime change and urged military, law enforcement, and security forces to join the people. He also spoke about plans for the post-Islamic Republic era, emphasizing maintaining security, fundamental freedoms, and meeting citizens' essential needs.

Videos released show that on Tuesday, 5 Aban, the anniversary of Sarina Saedi's death in the Mahsa uprising, families seeking justice for protesters killed in the "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests came to the grave of this teenage protester with pictures of their children.

Kylian Mbappé, the French star of Real Madrid, issued an official statement in three languages, apologizing to the people and history of China after a strong reaction from Chinese society and the cancellation of advertising contracts. He called his remarks about Mao Zedong as a "dictator" "clumsy." Mbappé wrote in his statement that his words were not his intention at all and that he has deep respect for the people and history of China.

Lithuania announced that two of its citizens were detained in Iran but refrained from disclosing their identities or details of the detention. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs received official information about the detentions from Iranian authorities on Tuesday, 5 Aban. Earlier, Lithuanian police reported the disappearance of two Lithuanian women in Iran, but the Ministry has not named the detained individuals.

Omid Shams, a lawyer and international affairs analyst, said that with the rise of any government in Israel, the military campaign against the Islamic Republic will continue, with differences in strategy and objectives. He identified the United States as the main decision-maker regarding the continuation or cessation of this operation.

Saud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar, in Moscow on Tuesday, 5 Aban. The meeting took place before the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit. Qatar, along with Pakistan, is trying to mediate between Tehran and Washington and to end conflicts in the Middle East.

Tehran Prosecutor's Office announced on Tuesday, 5 Aban, the arrest of a female sports blogger and the issuance of an arrest warrant for one of the organizers of the Fitex Tehran exhibition on charges of "behavior against norms and law". The blogger was arrested for publishing images and videos that, according to the prosecutor's office, hurt public sentiment and also "propaganda against the regime." An arrest warrant was also issued for another organizer involved in the design and planning of the event.
Maryam Jalal Hosseini, a political prisoner, returned to Kachouyi Prison in Karaj on Tuesday, 5 Aban, after completing a ten-day leave. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Mohammad Hassannejad, spokesperson for Tractor's board of directors, described the disciplinary committee's decision to declare his team the loser against Malavan as injustice and an engineered ruling. He said this ruling ended up benefiting competitors in the championship race and criticized that the punishment for insults was only two games without spectators. Hassannejad also emphasized that this ruling affected his team's chances of winning the championship.

A reception hall in Aliabad Katul was sealed by order of the county prosecutor due to holding a ceremony described by judicial authorities as contrary to Islamic norms. The hall manager, his child, a blogger, and several guests of the ceremony were arrested.

France's representative to the UN Security Council stated that the reinstatement of the Security Council sanctions against the Islamic Republic is completely legal and all UN member states are obliged to comply. He said France and its European partners activated the process to reinstate sanctions in August 2025. He also emphasized that the issue of nuclear non-proliferation remains on the Security Council's agenda.

The prison sentence of Ali Alirezaei, an undergraduate student at Sharif University of Technology, was reduced to one year by the appeals court. Previously, he was sentenced to four years in prison by the primary court.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, stated that the agency has no information about Iran's uranium stockpiles after the attacks. He said the Islamic Republic has not provided the information required by the agency. Grossi added that cooperation to clarify Iran's nuclear file continues, but some issues have remained unanswered for three years.
A video sent to Iran International shows students sticking papers on a school wall with the names of protesters killed by the Islamic Republic written on them.

It was reported that Yashar Tabrizi, a political prisoner in Tabriz prison, was transferred to solitary confinement five days ago and has been deprived of phone contact and visits with his family. This news was confirmed by a source close to the family.

Forough Kenani, a sociology researcher, described Prince Reza Pahlavi's call to join the "National Cooperation Campaign to Save Iran" as part of the "maximum organization" strategy. She emphasized the importance of organization to reduce repression and prevent a power vacuum during the transition period.

Shayan Samiei, a national security expert, said mediators no longer consider the Islamic Republic's promises sufficient and demand a change in its behavior. He emphasized that continuing negotiations does not mean the crisis is over.

The selection of Harry Kane as the winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or sparked a wave of praise in global media. British media considered this success the end of a 25-year wait, and German press praised Vincent Kompany's role in his development. Some Madrid and Catalan media reacted critically to this choice.

Ibrahim Sultan Al-Hashimi, Communications Director of Qatar's Foreign Ministry, said it is now Iran's turn to adhere to principles and show goodwill. He added that Iran must stop threats against the Arab countries of the Gulf region and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar and Pakistan are trying to mediate between Washington and Tehran to end the US and Israeli war against the Islamic Republic.

Jennifer Lotka, the US representative to the UN Security Council, stated on Tuesday, October 27, that the Islamic Republic's non-cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency is unacceptable. She said that the Islamic Republic has delayed the Agency's access to its most sensitive nuclear facilities for over a year and has refused to provide information and access to its highly enriched uranium reserves. Lotka welcomed the IAEA Board of Governors' decision to refer Iran's non-compliance with its safeguards obligations to the Security Council.

Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, met with Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the government of the Islamic Republic, on Tuesday, 5 Aban, at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum held in Moscow. The Gas Exporting Countries Forum has 12 members, and according to Russian officials, these countries hold 70% of the world's proven gas reserves, 38% of global gas production, and 42% of global gas exports.

Iran International has obtained exclusive information and documents indicating that the coup of the IRGC intelligence oil sales network was completed with the return of Ali Akbar Pour-Ebrahim. He is the IRGC's appointed figure responsible for 11 billion dollars of stolen trust funds from oil sales.

Reza Mostafaei, a 26-year-old disabled resident of Dehdasht, was released from Dehdasht prison on bail. This news was confirmed to HRANA by a source close to his family. His release took place on Sunday, 3 Aban [2026-10-25].

The website Halvash reported on Tuesday, 5 Aban, that following an attack by individuals on the relief unit headquarters and police station 11 in Khash county, several military personnel were killed and parts of the main streets of the city were blocked. The Mizan news agency, affiliated with the judiciary of the Islamic Republic, quoted the head of Khash police as saying that two armed individuals fired at the relief unit headquarters in this county and then fled the scene. The Mizan report did not mention any possible casualties from this attack.

Mostafa Nili, the lawyer of Jafar Panahi, announced that Branch 26 of Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced this director to five years and one month of imprisonment and confiscation of all movable and immovable properties. The sentence was issued in absentia. Panahi was also sentenced to two years of prohibition from social media activities and two years of travel ban.

October 11 is designated as the International Day of the Girl Child. This year, the day arrived amid unprecedented global turmoil, including wars, violence, and political unrest. Fundamentalism and authoritarian governments have intensified resistance against gender equality and efforts to protect girls' rights.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said in a meeting with Vladimir Putin that unilateral US actions in the region have highlighted the need to strengthen multilateralism and expand cooperation among sanctioned countries. He emphasized that regional countries have the ability to resolve disputes without relying on the US. Pezeshkian added that there is potential to expand comprehensive relations among regional countries in scientific, economic, industrial, cultural, security, and military fields.

Michael Carrick will remain Manchester United's coach despite eight consecutive matches without a win and the team's drop to sixteenth place in the English Premier League. The club's management decided to give Carrick another chance after a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth. Candidates like Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, and Julian Nagelsmann have not yet gained full approval from the management.

Leila Morvati, a political analyst, said that the victory of Benjamin Netanyahu's party would be the worst news for the Islamic Republic because in that case the unfinished project of Israel and the USA would end.

Meir Javdanfar said that Naftali Bennett pursued a direct confrontation policy with the Islamic Republic through the 'Octopus Doctrine' instead of focusing solely on its proxy forces. He added that Bennett managed to maintain Israel's relations with the US and Europe and prevented internal divisions. Javdanfar also criticized Netanyahu's policies and said Israel needs national cohesion, a strong economy, and greater participation of Haredi citizens in the army to effectively confront the Islamic Republic.

The death sentences of two prisoners previously convicted of murder and rape were carried out in the prisons of Shahr-e Kord and Kashan. Also, the death sentence of a couple residing in Kashmar in the case of the murder of a girl they had adopted was confirmed by the Supreme Court.

Voting in the Israeli parliamentary elections continues with participation reaching the highest level in half a century according to official statistics. Polls indicate a tight competition between Likud and Netanyahu's right-wing allies and the rival coalition led by Gadi Eisenkot.
A young worker employed at the industrial site of Kaveh Methanol Company in the city of Dir died on Monday, 4 Aban, after falling from a height.

A young woman in Tehran was targeted with acid attack on her car after rejecting a marriage proposal from a man she had previously been in contact with. The man threatened that if she refuses marriage, he will throw acid on her face. A case has been filed at Tehran's criminal court and investigations to arrest the suspect are ongoing.

Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Emir of Qatar, said in a meeting with Vladimir Putin that the Middle East is going through difficult conditions due to tensions between Tehran and Washington. The meeting was held at the Kremlin Palace. Putin stated that Russia is ready to make every effort to resolve the complex situation in the Middle East and highlighted Qatar's role as a mediator in Gulf region crises.

Voting is underway in Israel's first parliamentary elections since the Hamas attack on October 7. According to official statistics, turnout has reached the highest level in half a century. Benjamin Netanyahu, with public support from Donald Trump, has urged his supporters to prevent rivals from winning by voting in large numbers.

Tractor club protested the disciplinary committee's ruling regarding the match against Malavan and announced it will pursue the case in domestic and international bodies. The disciplinary committee declared the match result as 3-0 in favor of Malavan and deducted two points from Tractor. Tractor called this ruling a dangerous precedent and demanded a review of the referee and organizers' performance.

Esteghlal lost 2-0 to Shabab Al Ahli UAE in the third week of the Asian Elite League, experiencing their first defeat in the competition. Sardar Azmoun played a key role in Shabab Al Ahli's victory, assisting both goals. Esteghlal will face Al Shamal Qatar in their fourth match on Tuesday, 12 Aban in Basra, Iraq.
On Tuesday, 5 Aban 1405, a group of employees of Gachsaran Oil and Gas Company held a protest gathering in front of the company's central building, demanding attention to their demands.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said in the Cheshmandaz program that initial unofficial estimates are published after the end of the Israeli election voting and have usually been reliable. He referred to the broad political and media impact of the election on Europe and the United States.

Today, Tuesday, October 27, 2026, a number of contract workers of Gachsaran Oil and Gas Company, as well as retirees and pensioners of Iran Air (Homa), gathered to protest medical problems and the halt in payment of living and welfare allowances. Also, a group of workers from Navid Babakan contracting company protested the non-implementation of the status conversion plan in front of the Shahrbabak governorate. Yesterday, about 150 transferred workers of Khusheh Saba Agro-Industry Company gathered in Khoda Afarin county to protest several years of unpaid demands, and a number of independent bakeries in Iranshahr went on strike due to a reduction in their flour quota.

The UK Foreign Office has updated its travel warnings for 15 Middle Eastern countries, including Iran, declaring the region's security situation "highly unpredictable." The ministry warned that the risk of a sudden escalation of tensions is high, and Iran has stated its intention to target locations associated with the US and Israel. In this update, responsibility for attacks has been attributed to "Iran and others."

Israel's Central Elections Committee rejected requests from the Likud, Shas, and Otzma Yehudit parties to extend voting hours in the parliamentary elections, stating that voting would conclude as scheduled at 10 PM local time. The committee announced after reviewing the requests that, given the current conditions and high voter turnout, there was no justification for extending voting hours. The Central Elections Committee also emphasized that individuals in line by the time polling stations close would still be able to cast their votes.
Three candidates for Israel's prime minister and three approaches towards the Islamic Republic have been presented.

Amin Pardal, a 23-year-old Baloch citizen from Iranshahr, has been sentenced to death after a forced confession under physical and psychological torture and is at risk of execution. Basij agents went to a house where Pardal was a guest on 15 Farvardin and he disappeared after leaving the house to talk with them. His family met him after two months of no news and saw signs of bruising and torture on his body.

Reza Valizadeh, a journalist imprisoned in Evin Prison, is deprived of adequate medical care despite multiple physical problems and doctors' diagnosis requiring surgery and specialized tests. About six months have passed since his referral to the hospital was prescribed, but the transfer permit has not yet been issued.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the ancestral home of Reza Shah in Alasht, Mazandaran, which has been turned into an ethnographic museum, and said the doors of the house are closed and visitors are not allowed.
Mahnaz Ebrahimi, a math teacher and teachers' union activist in Shiraz, was arrested by security forces and transferred to Adelabad prison in the city.

Vladimir Putin, the President of Russia, expressed concern about the regional situation and developments related to Iran in a meeting with Masoud Pezeshkian. He also told the Emir of Qatar that the Islamabad agreement remains a basis for advancing negotiations to resolve the Iran crisis.

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, told Iran International that the US economic 'expulsion' operation will be 'even more severe' in the next eight weeks. He promised to further restrict Iran's air connections with the world and target the elites of the Islamic Republic and the Revolutionary Guards.

Israel's Channel 12 estimates that Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has 50 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority. The Change bloc led by Gadi Eizenkot has 52 seats, and Arab parties have 18 seats. Eizenkot announced he will act immediately to replace Netanyahu's government.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, on Tuesday, 5 Aban, urged citizens to participate widely in the elections and warned that low turnout could pave the way for the formation of a "left-wing government supported by Arab parties." The Central Elections Committee of Israel announced that in the first 9 hours of voting, 55.7 percent of eligible voters cast their ballots, a record high for this time period.

Persepolis club announced it intends to pursue the case regarding Yaser Asani's presence in Esteghlal's lineup at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) after the Football Federation's Appeals Committee rejected their complaint. Persepolis stated that international follow-up of the case had previously been approved by the board, and now with the Appeals Committee's ruling, the next steps of the complaint are underway. A meeting is scheduled on Wednesday with club managers and legal advisors to review legal aspects and expedite preparation of the complaint for referral to CAS.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, criticized the referee's performance after his team's 2-0 loss to Shabab Al Ahli UAE in the AFC Champions League, attributing the difference between the teams to their use of scoring opportunities. He apologized to the fans and said the team had faced tough matches recently. Bakhtiarizadeh also defended Esteghlal's more defensive play and strongly criticized the match officiating.

After the polls closed in Israel on the evening of Tuesday, 5 Aban, some citizens and party supporters in various locations, including Tel Aviv, took to the streets and celebrated alongside the announcement of probable results. These polls indicate a close competition with no definitive winner. Vote counting continues and the final result announcement may take several days.

Gadi Eizenkot, leader of the Yesh Atid party in Israel, considered the exit poll results from the parliamentary elections on Tuesday, 5 Aban, as a sign of the majority of Israeli citizens' vote of no confidence in Benjamin Netanyahu and his government. He promised to act to replace Netanyahu's government and form a Zionist government committed to universal mandatory military service. According to initial polls, the opposition coalition to Netanyahu is ahead of his supporting coalition, but neither coalition has reached the majority of 61 seats needed to form a government.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said the Islamic Republic hopes Benjamin Netanyahu will lose in the Israeli elections because it fears his continued cooperation with Donald Trump against Tehran. Vaisi added that in recent months, the Islamic Republic has tried to influence the US midterm elections by intensifying attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and raising oil prices. He also said Netanyahu's possible departure is more psychologically significant for the regime and that the final election result depends on vote counting and coalition negotiations.

Initial exit poll estimates in the Israeli parliamentary elections indicate that neither of the two main political blocs has secured the majority needed to form a government. The coalition led by Benjamin Netanyahu is estimated to win between 50 and 60 seats, while opposition parties are estimated to win between 43 and 52 seats out of 120 Knesset seats. These results indicate a political deadlock as neither Netanyahu nor his rival has a clear path to form a government.

The HalVash human rights group reported, by publishing videos, that armed individuals attacked the Relief Unit headquarters and Police Station 11 in Khash on Tuesday, October 27, and heavy clashes and shooting, including with machine guns, continued for over an hour. According to HalVash, local sources reported that a number of military forces were killed and injured, and official authorities have not yet announced any statistics on the number of dead and injured.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel, said that confronting the threats of the Islamic Republic and weakening its capabilities is a common point among Israel's main political currents. He added that part of the plans to confront Tehran were designed during the terms of Naftali Bennett and Gadi Eisenkot, and the parties' disagreements are mostly about how to implement these policies. Sabti also said that Benjamin Netanyahu's political behavior and humiliating treatment of his opponents have helped unite his rivals, and he did not rule out the possibility of Netanyahu forming a new coalition, but emphasized that the election results and negotiations among parties will determine the composition of Israel's future government.

Kambiz Tavana, a reporter for Iran International, said that discrepancies among exit polls in the Israeli elections have made predicting the composition of the future government difficult. He added that the formation of the government by Benjamin Netanyahu or his opponents, as well as the possibility of a political deadlock, remain topics of discussion. Tavana emphasized that the final result depends on the vote count and coalition negotiations, and it is still unclear who will form the future government.

Meir Javdanfar said that if the Islamic Republic falls, diplomatic relations between Iran and Israel could be quickly established, and Turkey and Qatar are concerned about this development. He added that the Israeli people's view of Iranians is positive and the historical and cultural ties between the two nations remain important. Javdanfar also said that Gadi Eizenkot needs to reach agreements with other parties, including Arab parties, to form a government, and the possible presence of Arab parties could change Israel's diplomatic image, but political disagreements and opposition from Haredi factions to military service will be major challenges for the government.

In today's Israeli parliamentary elections, Benjamin Netanyahu faced Gadi Eisenkot, the former Chief of Staff of the Israeli army. Eisenkot has gained more support in polls in recent months. His party has become one of the main rivals of the Likud party.

Mike Waltz, the US representative to the United Nations, addressed corruption in the Cuban government during the UN General Assembly, mentioning issues such as "luxury watches" and the private island "Cayo Piedra." These remarks provoked a strong reaction from the Cuban delegation, who protested by banging on the table. Khalil al-Rahman, the President of the General Assembly, suspended the session briefly following these reactions.

Reuters reported that Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, is expected to face questions about Washington's commitment to its obligations in the Indo-Pacific region during his meeting with counterparts from Southeast Asian countries in the Philippines on Wednesday, 6 Aban. The Iran war has pressured US military readiness and tensions between the Philippines and China in the South China Sea have increased. Analysts said Southeast Asian countries may use the meeting with Hegseth to clarify US goals in the Iran war and its impact on Washington's commitments in the region.

Donald Trump said in a campaign speech in Texas that the war with Iran will end whenever he wants and emphasized that the war will end soon. He added that it must be ensured that the world's biggest supporter of terrorism never obtains nuclear weapons. Trump has previously repeatedly spoken about the war's imminent end and stressed that the Islamic Republic should not acquire nuclear weapons.

The latest exit polls of the Israeli elections indicate an improvement in Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition position. Channel 12 reported the lead of Netanyahu's supporting coalition, while Channels 11 and 13 predicted a tie between the two main coalitions. Neither side has reached the majority needed to form a government.

An oil slick caused by damage to an oil tanker off the coast of the United Arab Emirates has expanded, leading to the closure of more beaches. Videos published on social media on October 26 and 27 show a closed beach in Ras Al Khaimah. Authorities in the emirate had announced on Saturday that all its beaches would be closed until further notice.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, after the release of exit poll results in the parliamentary elections, said Israel faces a historic opportunity to eliminate the threat of the Islamic Republic. He stated that the right-wing coalition has gained a decisive majority and that Iran is weaker than ever. Netanyahu also said Israel, together with Donald Trump, will end the threat from Iran once and for all.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US has informed several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a possible short but intense military operation against the Islamic Republic after the US midterm elections. The newspaper wrote that the US military is moving a Patriot missile system from Texas to strengthen its missile defense and relocating forces from vulnerable bases. Also, Donald Trump has not made a final decision but favors a large-scale attack after the elections that could target Iran's infrastructure and nuclear facilities.

Exit poll results published by Israel's Channel 12, Channel 14, and i24 News indicate the lead of Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, but there is an eight-seat discrepancy regarding the number of seats for this coalition. According to Channel 14's poll, Netanyahu's coalition will win 60 out of 120 Knesset seats. However, none of these polls show Netanyahu's coalition reaching the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government alone.

The first exit polls in the Israeli parliamentary elections show that opposition parties to Netanyahu win 52 to 53 seats, and his supporting coalition wins about 50 seats; thus, neither camp reaches the 61-seat threshold to form a government.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a Middle East analyst, says that a change of government in Israel may alter the timing, intensity, and method of operations against the Islamic Republic, but it does not fundamentally change Israel's security strategy towards Tehran. He states that confronting the missile and nuclear programs of the Islamic Republic and its security threats is pursued beyond electoral calculations and party politics in Israel.

Sadegh Beigdeli said that although the Israeli Prime Minister can influence tactics and some important decisions, the main strategy of Israel towards the Islamic Republic will not fundamentally change with a change of government. He added that currently, the Israeli army and security agencies such as Mossad and Shin Bet have a more prominent role in decision-making.

Kambiz Tavana, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the meeting between Masoud Pezeshkian and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, despite discussing energy cooperation, did not lead to a tangible agreement in this area. According to him, the only announced agreement was the reopening of the Russian state network VGTRK's office in Tehran, and there was no clear sign of practical action by Moscow to help Tehran against US economic pressures.

Prisoners participating in the "Tuesdays Against Execution" campaign went on a hunger strike in 66 prisons across Iran during the 144th week of the campaign. According to the campaign's statement, at least 87 people have been executed in Iran in the past 20 days, including seven political prisoners and two women. An interview with Pegah Bani Hashemi, a senior legal researcher at the University of Chicago, discussed the increase in execution rates and concerns of activists and human rights organizations.

The Parliament of South Australia held a ceremony to commemorate those who lost their lives for freedom in Iran. Parliament members condemned the suppression of protesters by the Islamic Republic during the ceremony. They called for an end to executions and the release of political prisoners.
